knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

## Introduction

This notebook is designed to help you interactively test the core functions of the `XploreQuran` package during active development. It uses `devtools::load_all()` to load your local package functions, allowing you to quickly test any code changes you make without needing to constantly rebuild the package.

## 1. Load the Package Development Environment

Run the following chunk to load all exported and internal functions directly from your `R/` directory.

```{r load-package}
# Load the package directly from source
# This ensures that any changes you make in the R/ directory are immediately available here.
devtools::load_all()

# Load necessary dependencies
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 2. Accessing Translation Data

The package works primarily with "translationList" objects. We can either load built-in data or pull new data from `tanzil.net` using the `tanzil_translation()` function.

### A. Using Built-in Data

The package should have some built-in data like `trans_en_sahih`. Let's load it and inspect it.

```{r load-builtin-data}
# Try loading built-in dataset
if (exists("trans_en_sahih") || try(data(trans_en_sahih, package = "XploreQuran"), silent = TRUE) == "trans_en_sahih") {
  print(class(trans_en_sahih))
  print(head(trans_en_sahih$translation_text))
  print(trans_en_sahih$translation_info)
} else {
  message("Built-in trans_en_sahih not found. Proceeding with download example.")
}
```

### B. Pulling Translation from Tanzil.net

You can test pulling a new translation. Here we pull the Malay translation.
*Note: This requires an active internet connection.*

```{r pull-translation, eval=FALSE}
# Example of pulling a new translation. We set eval=FALSE so it doesn't download every time you knit.
# Remove eval=FALSE or run interactively to test.
message("Downloading Malay Basmeih translation...")
trans_ms <- tanzil_translation("https://tanzil.net/trans/ms.basmeih")

print(class(trans_ms))
print(head(trans_ms$translation_text))
print(trans_ms$translation_info)
```

## 3. Creating Analytic Configurations

The core architecture of XploreQuran relies on the `TransAnalyticConfig` object, created via `trans_analytic_config()`. This dictates how the translation text is subsetted and preprocessed.

```{r test-config}
# 1. Default Configuration (All Surahs, English, Unigram)
cfg_default <- trans_analytic_config()
print(cfg_default)

# 2. Config for Juz 30 only, Bigrams, Stopwords removed
cfg_juz30_bigram <- trans_analytic_config(
  by = "juz", 
  sub_by = 30, 
  ngram = "bigram", 
  top_n = 15,
  remove_stopwords = TRUE,
  stopword_lang = "en"
)
print(cfg_juz30_bigram)

# 3. Config for Surah Al-Fatihah (1) and Al-Baqarah (2)
cfg_surah1_2 <- trans_analytic_config(
  by = "surah", 
  sub_by = c(1, 2), 
  ngram = "unigram", 
  top_n = 10
)
print(cfg_surah1_2)
```

## 4. Analyzing Term Frequency (TF-IDF)

Now let's test the `tf_trans()` function, which relies on your config object.

```{r test-tf-trans}
# Assuming trans_en_sahih is available. If not, make sure you ran the download chunk and replace the variable.
if (exists("trans_en_sahih")) {
  
  message("Testing Default TF-IDF Analysis...")
  tf_results <- tf_trans(trans_en_sahih, config = cfg_default)
  
  # Print the top rows
  print(head(tf_results, 10))
  
  # Quick visualization test
  # Let's plot the top terms for Surah Al-Fatihah
  tf_results %>%
    filter(surah_id == 1) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(word, tf), y = tf)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = "Top Terms in Surah Al-Fatihah (English Sahih)", x = "Word", y = "Term Frequency")
}
```

```{r test-tf-trans-bigram}
if (exists("trans_en_sahih")) {
  message("Testing Juz 30 Bigram Analysis...")
  tf_bigram_results <- tf_trans(trans_en_sahih, config = cfg_juz30_bigram)
  
  print(head(tf_bigram_results, 10))
}
```

## 5. Generating Wordclouds

Finally, test the `wordcloud_trans()` function.

```{r test-wordcloud}
if (exists("trans_en_sahih")) {
  
  message("Generating Wordcloud for Surah 1 & 2...")
  
  # Set up plot window size roughly
  par(mar = rep(0, 4))
  
  # Generate the wordcloud. The function also invisibly returns the frequency data.
  wc_data <- wordcloud_trans(
    tanzil_trans_object = trans_en_sahih, 
    config = cfg_surah1_2, 
    max_word = 100
  )
  
  # Preview the returned frequency data
  print(head(wc_data))
}
```

## 6. Testing Sentiment Analysis

The newly added `sentiment_trans()` function processes word sentiment across the text using lexicons (Bing, NRC, AFINN). Note that sentiment analysis requires the `ngram` setting to be "unigram".

```{r test-sentiment}
if (exists("trans_en_sahih")) {
  
  message("Testing Sentiment Analysis (Bing Lexicon) on Surah 1 & 2...")
  
  # Ensure unigram config
  cfg_sentiment <- trans_analytic_config(by = "surah", sub_by = c(1, 2), ngram = "unigram")
  
  # 1. Run the function
  sentiment_res <- sentiment_trans(
    tanzil_trans_object = trans_en_sahih, 
    config = cfg_sentiment, 
    lexicon = "bing", 
    index = "ayah"
  )
  
  # 2. View the custom print output
  print(sentiment_res)
  
  # 3. View the detailed analytical summary
  summary(sentiment_res)
  
  # 4. Plot the sentiment trajectory
  plot(sentiment_res)
}
```

## Conclusion and Next Steps

This notebook covers the complete backend analytical pipeline of `XploreQuran`. As you modify functions like `preprocess_tokens.R` or `trans_analytic_config.R`, you can simply rerun the `devtools::load_all()` chunk and run these specific blocks to instantly see if your changes broke any downstream analyses.

To test the Shiny App interface, you can run:

```{r launch-app, eval=FALSE}
# Run this interactively to launch the app
run_app()
```
